title: Product of Array Except Self
summary: You get a list of integers `nums`. Return a list `answer` of the same length where `answer[i]` is the product of every value in `nums` except itself, the one at index `i`. Solve it in O(n) time without using division. The returned list doesn't count as extra space; beyond it, aim for O(1).

examples.explanation: Every product that includes the 0 is 0; only answer[2] skips it: −1 × 2 × 3 = −6.

constraints: Every product of a run of values from either end fits in a 32-bit integer

approaches.twist: Fill answer with the product of everything left of i in one pass, then multiply in everything right of i in a backward pass.
Build a prefix-product array and a suffix-product array, then multiply the two at each index.
approaches.note: Works in O(n) time, but the two extra arrays take O(n) space. Keep the left products in answer itself and the right product in a single variable.

approaches.twist: For each index, loop over all the other values and multiply them together.
approaches.note: Works, but multiplying n − 1 values for each of n positions takes O(n²) time. The target is O(n).

signals.meaning: answer[i] splits into two pieces: the product of everything left of i and the product of everything right of i. Each piece is a running product you can carry through a pass.
Multiplying everything and dividing by nums[i] is ruled out, and it would break on a 0 anyway. Build each answer from both sides instead.
The answer list itself can hold the left products, and one variable can carry the right product, so no second array is needed.

constraintReading: len(nums) can reach 10⁵, so multiplying the other n − 1 values for every index is about 10¹⁰ steps: O(n²) is far too slow. O(n) means each index gets its product from running values. The O(1) space target (the answer list aside) rules out separate prefix and suffix arrays, so the answer list holds the left products and a single variable carries the right ones.

hints.clarify: Does `answer[i]` include `nums[i]` itself? No: it's everything else. Try [3, 2, 5] by hand: answer[0] = 2 × 5 = 10, answer[1] = 3 × 5 = 15, answer[2] = 3 × 2 = 6. Now try [3, 0, 5]: every answer that includes the 0 is 0, so only answer[1] = 15 survives. That's why dividing the total by `nums[i]` can't work.
hints.approach: Prefix scan in two directions. Everything except index i is the values left of i times the values right of i. Walk left to right with a running product `left`, starting at 1: write it into `answer[i]` first, then multiply `nums[i]` in. Then walk right to left with a running product `right`, also starting at 1: multiply it into `answer[i]`, then multiply `nums[i]` in. Each value is skipped exactly at its own index, because it's folded in only after its index has been written.
hints.whyNot: Multiplying the other values for each index is O(n²). Dividing the product of everything by `nums[i]` is not allowed, and it fails when `nums` holds a 0. Separate prefix and suffix arrays give the right answer in O(n) time, but they use O(n) extra space; the answer list can hold one side and a variable the other.

slots.setup: An answer list of n ones, and a running product `left` = 1: the product of nothing yet. Later, a second running product `right` = 1 for the backward pass.
slots.loop: Two passes: indexes 0 to n − 1 for the left products, then n − 1 down to 0 for the right products.
slots.update: After index i has been written, multiply `nums[i]` into the running product, so it covers one more value for the next index.
slots.record: In the forward pass, set `answer[i]` to `left` before folding `nums[i]` in. In the backward pass, multiply `answer[i]` by `right`, again before folding `nums[i]` in.
slots.return: After the backward pass, each `answer[i]` is the left product times the right product. Return the list.

solution.explanation: Two passes over n values with O(1) work at each step: O(n) time. Apart from the answer list, which the problem doesn't count, only `left`, `right` and `i` are stored: O(1) extra space. Writing `answer[i]` before multiplying `nums[i]` in is what leaves out the value at i: on the way forward, `left` holds the product of `nums[0..i-1]`, and on the way back, `right` holds the product of `nums[i+1..n-1]`.

events.label: left
events.say: Everything left of index {i} multiplies to {left}, so answer[{i}] starts as {left}

events.label: right
events.say: Everything right of index {i} multiplies to {right}, so answer[{i}] becomes {answer[i]} × {right} = {answer[i] * right}

events.label: return
events.say: Every answer[i] is now its left product times its right product: {answer}

predict.ask: What will left be once nums[i] is folded in?
What will right be once nums[i] is folded in?

related.relation: Also carries one running value through a single pass, the lowest price so far, and reads each day's answer from it.
Also needs what lies on both sides of each index, but takes running maximums instead of running products, and gets O(1) space with two pointers.
